items.question: Where and with what care must this teaching be kept hidden?
premises: The teaching must be concealed
Concealment requires deliberate effort
The mortal world contains the lowest of men
items.inference: This teaching must be carefully concealed in the mortal world among the lowest of men.
items.plain_english: It must be carefully concealed in the mortal world among the lowest of men.

items.question: To whom and after what testing may this teaching be given?
premises: The teaching may be given
The recipient should be previously accomplished
The recipient must be tested for one year
items.inference: This teaching should be given only to a previously accomplished person who has been tested for one year.
items.plain_english: It should be given to one who is already accomplished and has been tested for one year.

items.question: Which chapter concludes in the text emerged from Candradvīpa?
premises: The text is identified as emerged from Candradvīpa
A chapter is being numbered
The ordinal is fifth
items.inference: The fifth chapter in the text emerged from Candradvīpa concludes here.
items.plain_english: Thus ends the fifth chapter in the text that emerged from Candradvīpa.

items.question: What understanding has been attained through the grace of the lord of Kaulas?
premises: The speaker addresses the lord of Kaulas
Knowledge has arisen by his grace
The object known is the determination of Kaula
items.inference: By the grace of the lord of Kaulas, the speaker has come to know the determination of Kaula.
items.plain_english: O lord of Kaulas, by your grace I have come to know the determination of the Kaula teaching.

items.question: What is the declared identity and essential nature of the individual soul?
premises: The soul has been declared in the teaching
Its identity is being questioned
Its essential nature is also being questioned
items.inference: The verse asks who the declared soul is and what its essential nature is.
items.plain_english: Who is that soul that has been declared, and what is the nature of the soul?

items.question: Into what does the soul dissolve, and what full explanation is requested?
premises: The soul undergoes dissolution
The locus of dissolution is questioned
The speaker requests a complete explanation
items.inference: The verse asks into what the soul dissolves and requests that all this be explained.
items.plain_english: And into what does it dissolve? Tell me all of that.

items.question: What supreme qualities define the true nature of that soul?
premises: The soul is identified as supreme
The soul is described as partless and eternal
The soul is free from disease and stainless
items.inference: The soul is supreme, partless, eternal, free from disease, and stainless.
uncertainties: Gender agreement appears neuter in predicates though jīva is masculine; taken as describing its essence.
items.plain_english: It is supreme, partless, eternal, free from disease, and stainless.

items.question: How is the transcendent soul identified as haṃsa and the individual of power?
premises: The soul is described as supremely transcendent
That soul is identified as haṃsa
That soul is also identified as the individual of power
items.inference: The supremely transcendent soul is identified as haṃsa, the individual of power.
uncertainties: The exact doctrinal sense of śakti+pudgalaḥ is context-dependent.
items.plain_english: That soul which is supremely transcendent is the haṃsa, the individual of power.

items.question: In what form and where is the vital air said to be situated?
premises: The vital air is filled with breath
It is situated in all beings
Its presence is affirmed as established
items.inference: The breath-filled vital air is situated in all living beings.
uncertainties: Agreement of saṃsthitam (neuter) with vāyuḥ (masculine) is irregular; read as describing the state.
items.plain_english: The breath-filled vital air is situated in all living beings.

items.question: What is the soul called immediately upon leaving the body?
premises: The soul leaves the body
This departure is described as mere or immediate
Upon departure it is designated supreme Śiva
items.inference: As soon as it leaves the body, the soul is called supreme Śiva.
items.plain_english: As soon as it leaves the body, it is called the supreme Śiva.

items.question: How is this teaching heard and transmitted according to tradition?
premises: The teaching is heard in the ear
It comes down through a lineage
The goddess is addressed as recipient
items.inference: This teaching is heard in the ear, having come down through the succession of tradition.
items.plain_english: O goddess, it is heard in the ear, having come down through the succession of tradition.

items.question: What effect arises from merely hearing this knowledge?
premises: The knowledge is merely heard
Hearing itself is presented as sufficient
The fair-faced goddess is addressed
items.inference: By merely hearing this knowledge, a significant effect is implied for the practitioner.
uncertainties: The verse is syntactically incomplete and continues into the next verse.
items.plain_english: O fair-faced one, by merely hearing this knowledge...

rows.grounds: object; may refer to renunciant state

items.question: What practice over six months leads to a state free from bondage?
premises: Practice is prescribed for six months
The practitioner attains an ochre or renunciant state
That state is free from bondage
items.inference: One who practices for six months attains a renunciant state free from bondage.
uncertainties: The exact sense of kāṣāyaṃ here (ochre robe or ascetic state) is interpretive.
items.plain_english: But whoever practices for six months attains the ochre state, free from bondage.

items.question: What liberation and companionship result from this sustained practice?
premises: The practitioner becomes freed from all diseases
The practitioner gains association with yogis
Union with yogis is presented as an outcome
items.inference: Through this practice one becomes free from all diseases and attains union with yogis.
uncertainties: The syntactic role of saha+melakam is compressed; read as attaining union.
items.plain_english: Freed from all diseases, he attains union together with the yogis.

items.question: What teaching about the practice concerning the soul has now been conveyed?
premises: A teaching has been told to the listener
The subject is the practice of the soul
Bhairavī is addressed directly
items.inference: The practice concerning the soul has now been explained to Bhairavī.
items.plain_english: O Bhairavī, this practice concerning the soul has been told to you.

items.question: To what kind of resolved recipient may this teaching be given?
premises: The teaching may be given
The recipient is endowed with all states
The recipient has a resolved mind
items.inference: This teaching should be given to one endowed with all states and of resolved mind.
uncertainties: The case usage is compressed; both qualifiers describe the worthy recipient.
items.plain_english: It should be given to one who is endowed with all states and has a resolved mind.

items.question: To whom must the essential Kaula teaching originating from the yoginīs not be given?
premises: The Kaula essence is highly valued
It originates from the yoginīs
It must not be given indiscriminately
items.inference: The essential Kaula teaching, originating from the yoginīs, must not be given to the unworthy.
uncertainties: The intended unworthy recipient is implied rather than explicitly named.
items.plain_english: The essential Kaula teaching, which originates from the yoginīs, must not be given.

items.question: What transformation of the body from ignorance to purity is being claimed now?
premises: The speaker refers to the present moment
The body was struck by the veil of ignorance
The body is now described as pure
items.inference: The speaker claims that her body, once struck by ignorance, is now pure.
uncertainties: The syntax is compressed; read as a statement of realized purification.
items.plain_english: Today my body, once struck by the veil of ignorance, is pure.

items.question: What auspicious method for overcoming time does the speaker now wish to hear?
premises: The speaker expresses a present wish
The desired topic concerns time
The goal is the auspicious overcoming of time
items.inference: The speaker now wishes to hear the auspicious means of overcoming time.
uncertainties: vañcanaṃ can mean deception or eluding; rendered as overcoming in this context.
items.plain_english: Now I wish to hear the auspicious means of overcoming time.

items.question: What assurance is given that death can truly be destroyed?
premises: The speaker promises to explain
There is said to be no doubt
The explanation concerns how death is destroyed
items.inference: The speaker asserts without doubt that death can be destroyed and will explain how.
items.plain_english: I shall tell you—there is no doubt—how death is destroyed.

items.question: What intense experience at the tip of nectar affects even the wise practitioner?
premises: The practice involves the tip of nectar
There is contact with the tip of essence
Even a wise person experiences burning
items.inference: Even the wise practitioner experiences a burning sensation at the tip of nectar through the tip of essence.
uncertainties: The physiological referents of amṛta+agraṃ and rasa+agreṇa are yogic and context-specific.
items.plain_english: Even the wise one experiences burning at the tip of nectar by means of the tip of essence.

items.question: How should the breath be drawn in at the root of tongue and palate?
premises: Attention is placed at the root of tongue and palate
The breath is the object of the practice
The breath should be drawn in slowly
items.inference: One should place awareness at the root of the tongue and palate and slowly drink in the breath.
items.plain_english: Placing awareness at the root of the tongue and palate, one should slowly drink in the breath.

items.question: What result follows from practicing this breath discipline for one year?
premises: The practice is continued for one year
The practice becomes firmly established
Old age and death are subject to destruction
items.inference: When this practice is maintained for one year, old age and death are destroyed.
items.plain_english: When practiced for one year, old age and death are destroyed.

items.question: What immunity to venom is claimed for one established in this practice?
premises: The practitioner may be bitten by great serpents
Poison would normally enter the body
In this case poison does not enter the body
items.inference: Even if bitten by great serpents, poison does not enter the body of such a practitioner.
items.plain_english: Even if bitten by great serpents, poison does not enter the body.
